newsitem.title: ITALY: More offers could come for Creditanstalt - Bd member.
newsitem.headline: More offers could come for Creditanstalt - Bd member.

text.p: More offers could still emerge for Austrian privatisation candidate Creditanstalt, a director of the bank said on Thursday.

"There are five more parties who could formulate an offer by the final deadline of December 15," Klaus Peschek told reporters at a presentation in Milan on the group's Italian subsidiary, Creditanstalt Finanziaria, which he chairs.

The Austrian finance ministry said on Monday that it had received two indicative offers for the government's 70 percent stake in Creditanstalt, at the top of its privatisation list for the past six years.
Interested parties have to make binding offers after the close of a two- to three-week due diligence period.

Only one of the two potential bidders, a group led by Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali, has been identified. The EA-Generali consortium comprises Commerzbank, Banca Commerciale Italiana, and Austrian bank Die Erste.
Peschek said he expected to be informed of the identity of the second potential bidder on December 4 when their due diligence period ended.
Peschek said he supported the EA-Generali bid. "It's in our interest that a hard core is formed with strong Italian and German partners with a view to European Union."

Creditanstalt could strengthen its position in BCI, in which it currently holds a 1.25 percent stake, Peschek said, adding: "In future it could be possible; in the last few years it has not been possible because of a conflict of interest with the privatisation process."
